name: multiple_answers: This is one of multiple questions about the same…
questionText: This is one of multiple questions about the same scenario. NCAA coaches may be compensated with salary as well as with an annual bonus. The amount of that bonus may be contingent on team performance as well as meeting off-field thresholds with respect to players' grades and conduct. The distribution of salary and bonus is something that coaches negotiate with the Athletic Director at a NCAA school. A college football coach-who-will-not-be-named is evaluating the job market and wants to predict what sort of bonus compensation he might expect to earn at various NCAA schools. Using NCAA Salaries data, he fits a model with the following variables: Bonus: maximum annual bonus (in millions of dollars) Salary: annual salary (in millions of dollars) SEC: whether the school is in the Southeastern Conference (SEC = 1) or not (SEC = 0) The model equation is: Which of the follow statements is accurate, in light of the fitted model? Select all correct answers.

choices.label: A
choices.text: This model incorporates an interaction term.

choices.label: B
choices.text: At both SEC schools and non-SEC schools, bonuses increase at a rate of $150,000 for a $1 million-increase in salary.

choices.label: C
choices.text: As salaries increase at SEC schools, bonuses also tend to increase. However, that increase is more slow and gradual than at non-SEC schools.

choices.label: D
choices.text: As salaries increase at SEC schools, bonuses tend to decrease.

name: multiple_choice: As an Advanced Accounting Analytics intern at Gringotts Bank,…
questionText: As an Advanced Accounting Analytics intern at Gringotts Bank, you are tasked with investigating factors that explain variation in credit card account balances. You are working with a data set with information on 400 credit card accounts, including the following variables: Balance: credit card balance, i.e. debt owed to bank ($ dollars) Income: cardholder annual income ($ thousands of dollars) Limit: credit spending limit ($ dollars) Student: Yes/No indicator for whether cardholder is a part- or full-time student, or else not a student You fit a linear regression model for Balance in terms of the following predictors: Income Limit Student the interaction between Student and Limit Then, you use the results of this model to generate standardized coefficients and intervals: Parameter | Coefficient (std.) | 95% CI------------------------------------------------------(Intercept) | -0.09 | [-0.12, -0.07]Income | -0.61 | [-0.65, -0.57]StudentYes | 0.93 | [ 0.86, 1.00]Limit | 1.33 | [ 1.30, 1.37]StudentYes:Limit | 0.16 | [ 0.09, 0.24] Based on the table above, which of the following conclusions below is accurate? Choose the best answer.

choices.label: A
choices.text: The relationship between balance and credit limit is not statistically significantly different for students versus non-students (adjusting for income).

choices.label: B
choices.text: None of the other answers is correct.

choices.label: C
choices.text: For non-student cardholders earning the same annual income, we expect a 1.33-standard deviation balance increase for a one-standard deviation increase in credit limit.

choices.label: D
choices.text: With 95% confidence, we estimate a balance decrease of as much as $0.65 for a one-dollar increase in cardholder annual income.

choices.label: E
choices.text: We are 95% confident that the main effect for the Student variable implies a balance increase of at least 86 cents.

name: multiple_choice: In Lesson 15.5, we fit a multiple regression model…
questionText: In Lesson 15.5, we fit a multiple regression model to predict the listing price of a house in Saratoga County, New York. We concluded that the variable age (age of the house in years) should be included in a model attempting to isolate the partial relationship between fireplaces and price. Which of the following is among the reasons that we decided to include age in the model? (1) The confidence interval for the age coefficient did not contain zero. (2) The inclusion of the age variable affected the magnitude of the coefficient of interest: fireplaces. (3) Age was correlated with both the response variable (price) and the predictor variable of interest (fireplaces).

questionText: A local grocery store collects data on daily sales of pints of guacamole. The following jitter plots shows sales versus two variables: whether it is a weekend or a weekday whether there are free samples of guacamole (No/Yes) The orange dots show the group means for each scenario. Which of the following statements is accurate, based on the visual evidence in the above plot? (1) The effect on sales of offering free samples looks larger on a weekend than it does on a weekday. (2) The effect on sales of offering free samples looks larger on a weekday than it does on a weekend. (3) A regression model to predict sales in terms of the weekend variable and the free samples variable should likely also include an interaction between these two predictors.

name: multiple_choice: Buildings that invest in energy efficiency reduce global-warming greenhouse…
questionText: Buildings that invest in energy efficiency reduce global-warming greenhouse gas emissions and costs associated with energy consumption. Sustainability may also be appealing to building tenants. Do “green-certified” buildings offer a premium on the commercial real-estate market? An analyst at an architecture firm uses data on 7,894 commercial buildings to fit a model predicting revenue per square foot by whether the building has a green rating, producing the following results: lm(rev_psf ~ green_rating, data=greenbuildings) %>% get_regression_table(digits=1) %>% select(-std_error:-p_value) Next, they fit the model with an additional predictor variable for building age in years: lm(rev_psf ~ green_rating + age, data=greenbuildings) %>% get_regression_table(digits=1) %>% select(-std_error:-p_value) Which of the following statements is accurate with respect to the results of these two regression models? (1) Both models suggest (with 95% confidence) that a green rating is associated with an increase in revenue. (2) The second model's green rating coefficient suggests that some of the green rating effect observed with the first model was, in fact, partially attributable to variation in building age. (3) The first model estimates an overall relationship between green rating and revenue.

name: multiple_choice: An EPA analyst works with a data frame containing…
questionText: An EPA analyst works with a data frame containing information on virtually every model of vehicle offered for sale to U.S. consumers during 2020, including the following variables: make -- one of 41 car manufacturers. The baseline category of this variable is Acura. city -- city gas mileage in miles per gallon highway -- highway gas mileage in miles per gallon displacement -- engine size in liters emissions -- emissions of carbon dioxide (CO2), measured in grams of CO2 per mile driven powertrain -- vehicle engine type: Diesel, EV, FFV, Gasoline, Hybrid, or Plug-in Hybrid category -- type of vehicle: Car, Small Car, SUV/Van, Truck, TwoSeater, Wagon They fit a regression model to predict highway gas mileage in terms of engine displacement and vehicle type category: lm(highway ~ displacement + category, data=cars) %>% get_regression_table(digits=1) %>% select(-std_error, -statistic, -p_value) producing the following results: Based on this regression table, which of the following statements is accurate? Choose the best answer.

choices.label: A
choices.text: For vehicles in the SUV/Van category, we expect a decrease of 7.5 highway miles-per-gallon for a one-liter increase in engine displacement.

choices.label: B
choices.text: We are 95% confident that vehicles in the Wagon category get between 0.2 and 3.3 fewer highway miles per gallon for a one-liter increase in engine displacement.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Vehicles in the Car category get between 38-40 highway miles-per-gallon.

choices.label: D
choices.text: When comparing vehicles with the same engine displacement, we expect a decrease in highway miles-per-gallon for each vehicle category relative to the baseline Car category.

questionText: This question revisits the data on video-game reaction time that we analyzed in class and in Lesson 14. Specifically, we'll consider three variables from this data set (two that we looked at before, and one that we didn't): PictureTarget.RT: the subject's reaction time in milliseconds when presented with a visual stimulus FarAway: a dummy variable for whether the stimulus (i.e. the “bad guy” popping up on the screen) was near (0) or far away (1) within the visual scene. SceneLetter: a letter code (b, c, d, e, or f) indicating which of five scenes the subject was presented with. (Note: the letters start at b; there is no scene a in this data set) Consider the following model and its corresponding regression table: lm(PictureTarget.RT ~ FarAway + SceneLetter, data=rxntime) %>% get_regression_table() %>% select(-std_error, -statistic, -p_value) Based on this model output, the predicted reaction time for scene e when FarAway=0 is closest to which of the following?

name: matching: There is a distinction between causal questions and statistical…
questionText: There is a distinction between causal questions and statistical questions. Causal questions are about cause and effect (i.e., questions about counterfactual statements). Statistical questions, on the other hand, are about correlations (i.e., patterns we observe with data). Identify each of the examples below as either a STATISTICAL sort of question or a CAUSAL sort of question:

blanks.label: If we invested more money in our school system, how much faster would our economy grow?
How are education spending and economic growth related in a data set representing many world countries?
If I ate more vegetables than I do now, how much longer would I live?
Do people who eat a lot of vegetables live longer, on average, than people who don’t?
If we hire extra teachers at our school and reduce our class sizes, will our students’ test scores improve?
Do students in smaller classes tend to have higher test scores?

name: multiple_choice: To what extent does a patient’s body mass index…
questionText: To what extent does a patient’s body mass index (bmi) predict the medical insurance charges for their care? The file insurance.csv contains data on 325 patients from the southwest region who incurred medical insurance charges, including the following variables: bmi: body mass index of patient charges: insurance charges for patient’s medical care in dollars Fit a linear model for charges (Y) in terms of bmi (X). Based on these model results, which of the following statements is accurate? (1) For a 10-point increase in patient bmi, we'd expect medical charges to increase by approximately $45.27. (2) For a patient with a bmi of 25, we would predict their medical charges to be approximately $9,800. (3) If a patient somehow had zero bmi, we’d expect their medical charges to be approximately -$1,503.

name: multiple_choice: Why is it useful to approximate the sampling distribution…
questionText: Why is it useful to approximate the sampling distribution of a statistical summary? Choose the best answer below.

choices.label: A
choices.text: The sampling distribution measures the repeatability of our answer in the presence of randomness, and therefore can be used to quantify our level of statistical uncertainty.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The sampling distribution can eliminate our uncertainty about how the results from a sample can be generalized to the wider population.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The sampling distribution is the variability in a measure that we observe in only one particular sample.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The sampling distribution can reduce our uncertainty about how the results from a sample can be generalized to the wider population.

questionText: O's Cafe offers a pizza lunch during which each customer selects exactly one slice of pizza, choosing either cheese or pepperoni. On a slow day with 40 customers, the probability that all 40 of them will choose cheese pizza is 1. * In other words, three out of every four slices selected are cheese; there is a 25% probability that a customer selects pepperoni.
